steps.title: Forced structure
steps.body:
$P$ and $S$ can come first in either order. $R$ needs both $P$ and $S$ before it, and $Q$ needs $R$ before it. So the only orders are

$$P\,S\,R\,Q \quad\text{and}\quad S\,P\,R\,Q.$$

cse-2014-1-cs-14.approach: With the first element as pivot, partitioning $n$ elements costs $n-1$ comparisons. A sorted input gives the worst case; the second input splits fairly evenly, so it needs fewer.

steps.title: Input [1 2 3 4 5]
steps.body:
Each pivot is the minimum, so every partition removes just one element:

$$t_1 = 4+3+2+1 = 10.$$

steps.title: Input [4 1 5 3 2]
steps.body:
Pivot 4: $4$ comparisons, giving $\{1,3,2\}$ and $\{5\}$. Sorting the 3-element part takes at most $2+1 = 3$ comparisons (pivot 1: $2$ comparisons, then $\{3,2\}$: $1$), and $\{5\}$ takes $0$.

$$t_2 \le 4 + 3 = 7.$$

optionAnalysis.reason: $t_1 = 10$, not 5: the sorted input is the worst case, $\binom{5}{2}=10$ comparisons.
The sorted input is the worst case, so $t_1$ cannot be smaller.
The second input splits $3:1$ at the top level and needs only about 7 comparisons.

pitfalls: Counting element swaps instead of comparisons.
cse-2014-1-cs-14.verification: Worst case for $n=5$ is $n(n-1)/2 = 10$; any other split is strictly cheaper.

cse-2014-1-cs-15.approach: A language is regular when a finite automaton only needs bounded memory. Counting modulo a constant needs finitely many states; matching counts, primes or copies does not.

steps.title: Option (C) is regular
steps.body: "Number of $b$'s is $3k+1$" means #$b \equiv 1 \pmod 3$. A 3-state DFA tracks #$b \bmod 3$ (self-loops on $a$) and accepts in state 1, e.g. $a^*b\,a^*\big(b\,a^*b\,a^*b\,a^*\big)^*$.

steps.title: The others are not
steps.body:
- $a^nb^n$: must remember $n$ — pumping inside the $a$ block breaks the balance.
- $\{a^p : p\text{ prime}\}$: unary regular languages have ultimately periodic lengths, primes are not.
- $ww$: pumping $0^n1\,0^n1$ in the first block destroys the copy.

Prime lengths are not ultimately periodic, so not regular (not even context-free).
Counting $b$'s modulo 3 needs only 3 states.
$ww$ needs unbounded memory to compare the halves; it is not even context-free.

$$\{E,F,H\}^+ = \{E,F,H,G,I,J,K,L,M,N\} = R.$$

It is minimal (it contains only the mandatory attributes), so it is **the** key — option (B).

cse-2014-1-cs-22.approach: Test each statement against SQL semantics: a foreign key must reference a key of the parent table, and foreign keys carry referential actions that a CHECK assertion cannot reproduce.

steps.title: S1 is false
steps.body: An assertion can only reject a violating state. A foreign key can also specify referential actions such as `ON DELETE CASCADE` / `SET NULL`, which repair the child table automatically — no CHECK assertion can do that. So a foreign key cannot **always** be replaced by an equivalent assertion.

steps.title: S2 is false
steps.body: `FOREIGN KEY (a) references R` refers to $R$'s primary key, which is the pair $(a, b)$. A single column cannot reference a two-column key (and $a$ alone is not unique in $R$). So the definition is invalid.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: Both S1 and S2 are false — option (D).

steps.title: Window for 60%
steps.body: $$\frac{W\,T_t}{T_t + 2T_p} \ge 0.6 \Rightarrow W \ge 0.6 \times \frac{105.46}{5.46} = 0.6 \times 19.31 \approx 11.6 \Rightarrow W = 12.$$

steps.body: Selective repeat needs $2W = 24$ sequence numbers: $\lceil\log_2 24\rceil = 5$ bits.
